_note: Seed question bank. Add questions here (or import via Admin > Data Import) - nothing is hardcoded in the UI. Types: mcq | multi | short | coding | written. 'checks' describes what the mocked code runner looks for; 'tests' lists real test cases used by a real sandbox runner if you plug one in.

questions.prompt: A number is increased by 20% and then decreased by 20%. The net change is:
questions.explanation: 1.20 x 0.80 = 0.96, so the value falls by 4%.

questions.prompt: In an exam, 35% failed in Maths and 25% failed in English. If 10% failed in both, what percentage passed in both subjects?
questions.explanation: Failed in at least one = 35 + 25 - 10 = 50%. So 50% passed in both.

questions.prompt: The price of sugar rises by 25%. By what percentage must a family reduce consumption to keep expenditure unchanged?
If a : b = 3 : 4 and b : c = 6 : 7, then a : c is:
Two vessels contain milk and water in ratios 3:1 and 5:3. In what ratio must they be mixed to obtain a mixture with milk and water in the ratio 2:1?
questions.explanation: Alligation on milk fractions 3/4 and 5/8 with mean 2/3 gives 1:2.

questions.prompt: A completes a job in 12 days and B in 18 days. Working together, how long will they take to complete 3 such jobs?
questions.explanation: Together one job = 36/5 = 7.2 days, so three jobs = 21.6 days.

questions.prompt: A train 150 m long crosses a platform 250 m long in 20 seconds. Its speed is:
questions.explanation: Distance = 400 m in 20 s = 20 m/s = 72 km/h.

questions.prompt: An article marked at Rs. 1200 is sold after two successive discounts of 10% and 5%. The selling price is:
What sum invested at 8% simple interest per annum earns Rs. 1440 as interest in 3 years?
The average age of 30 students is 15 years. A student aged 20 leaves the group. The new average is:
In how many ways can the letters of the word LEADER be arranged?
questions.explanation: 6! / 2! = 360 (E repeats twice).

questions.prompt: Two dice are thrown. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers is a prime number?
questions.explanation: 15 favourable outcomes out of 36 = 5/12.

questions.prompt: What is the remainder when 17^23 is divided by 16?
Find the HCF of 36 and 84. Enter the number only.
Find the next term: 4, 9, 19, 39, ?
questions.explanation: Each term = previous x 2 + 1, so 39 x 2 + 1 = 79.

questions.prompt: Find the missing term: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
questions.explanation: Differences 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 - so next is 42.

questions.prompt: Complete the series: AZ, BY, CX, DW, ?
questions.explanation: First letter moves forward, second backward: E then V.

questions.prompt: Statements: All engineers are graduates. Some graduates are managers. Conclusion: I. Some engineers are managers. II. Some managers are graduates. Which conclusions follow?
questions.explanation: Some graduates are managers converts to some managers are graduates; I is not forced.

questions.prompt: Statements: No laptop is a tablet. All tablets are phones. Conclusions: I. Some phones are not laptops. II. No laptop is a phone.
questions.explanation: Tablets are phones and no laptop is a tablet, so at least those phones are not laptops; II is not forced.

questions.prompt: Pointing to a photograph, Ravi says, "Her mother is the only daughter of my mother." How is the girl related to Ravi?
questions.explanation: The only daughter of Ravi's mother is Ravi's sister, so her daughter is Ravi's niece.

questions.prompt: A is B's brother. C is B's mother. D is C's father. E is D's mother. How is A related to D?
questions.explanation: D is A's grandfather, so A is D's grandson.

questions.prompt: A man walks 5 km north, turns right and walks 3 km, then turns right and walks 5 km. How far is he from the start?
questions.explanation: The north and south legs cancel; he is 3 km east of the start.

questions.prompt: A man walks 5 km north, turns right and walks 3 km, then turns right and walks 8 km. In which direction is he from the starting point?
questions.explanation: He ends 3 km east and 3 km south, i.e. south-east of the start.

questions.prompt: Five friends P, Q, R, S, T sit in a row facing north. Q is to the immediate right of P. T is at one end. S is between Q and T. Who sits in the middle?
questions.explanation: The order P Q S T with R placed gives Q as the middle seat.

questions.prompt: You have 8 identical balls, one heavier. Using a balance scale, the minimum number of weighings needed to guarantee finding it is:
questions.explanation: Weigh 3 vs 3; the heavier group or the remaining 2 identifies the ball in a second weighing.

questions.prompt: A family spends Rs. 40,000 per month: Rent 30%, Food 25%, Education 20%, Travel 15%, Savings 10%. By what percent is the rent higher than the savings?
questions.explanation: Rent Rs. 12,000 vs savings Rs. 4,000 - an increase of 200%.

questions.prompt: A company's revenue grew from Rs. 8 crore to Rs. 10 crore while costs grew from Rs. 6 crore to Rs. 8.4 crore. What happened to the profit margin?
questions.explanation: Margin fell from 25% (2/8) to 16% (1.6/10).

questions.prompt: If ROSE is coded as 6821, CHAIR as 73456 and PREACH as 961473, what is the code for SEARCH? (Enter the digits only)
questions.explanation: Mapping each letter from the two given codes gives S=2, E=1, A=4, R=6, C=7, H=3.

questions.prompt: What is the time complexity of binary search on a sorted array of n elements?
questions.explanation: The search space halves each step.

questions.prompt: An algorithm runs in O(n^2) with n = 10^4. Roughly how many basic operations does that imply?
questions.explanation: (10^4)^2 = 10^8 operations - too slow for a 1 second limit.

questions.prompt: Which approach finds the second largest element of an array in a single pass?
options: Track largest and second largest while scanning
questions.explanation: One pass with two running variables is O(n) time and O(1) space.

questions.prompt: Average-case lookup time in a well-implemented hash table is:
questions.explanation: Hashing gives constant average lookup, degrading to O(n) with heavy collisions.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are LIFO structures or operations best served by a stack? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: BFS uses a queue; the other three are classic stack use cases.

questions.prompt: The number of calls made by the naive recursive Fibonacci function for f(5) is:
questions.explanation: The call tree for f(5) makes 15 calls - the reason for memoisation.

questions.prompt: Which data structure best checks whether two strings are anagrams in O(n) time?
options: A frequency count array or map
questions.explanation: Counting character frequencies compares in linear time.

questions.prompt: Write a function that returns the second largest element in an array of integers. Return -1 if it does not exist. Complete the Java method.

checks.label: Uses a single loop or iteration
Tracks a second maximum and handles the no-answer case

questions.explanation: Track largest and secondLargest in one pass; if array length < 2 or all elements equal, return -1.

questions.prompt: Reverse the words in a sentence without reversing the characters inside each word. For "I love placements" the output is "placements love I".
questions.explanation: Split on whitespace, then rebuild in reverse order.

questions.prompt: Check whether a number is an Armstrong number (sum of its digits each raised to the power of the digit count equals the number). Return true for 153.

checks.label: Raises digits to the power of the digit count

questions.explanation: Count digits first, then accumulate each digit raised to that count.

questions.prompt: Print a right-angled star pattern of n rows, each row i having i stars. Return the pattern as a single string with \n between rows.

checks.label: Uses loops for rows and columns

questions.explanation: An outer loop over rows and an inner loop over columns.

questions.prompt: Given a sorted array and a target, return the index of the target using binary search, or -1 if absent.
questions.explanation: Maintain low/high pointers and halve the range each step.

questions.prompt: Return the first non-repeating character in a string, or '#' if every character repeats.

checks.label: Uses a hash map or frequency array

questions.explanation: Count frequencies in one pass, then scan again for the first count of one.

questions.prompt: Print all permutations of a string without duplicates. Return the count of distinct permutations for "AAB".
questions.explanation: Backtrack with a used[] marker, or simply use n! / product of repeated factorials = 3!/2! = 3.

questions.prompt: Maximum sum of a non-adjacent subsequence in an array. For [5, 1, 1, 5] the answer is 10 (take 5 and 5).
questions.explanation: include = exclude + a[i]; exclude = max(include, exclude) carried forward.

questions.prompt: Choose the grammatically correct sentence:
options: Each of the students have submitted the assignment.
Each of the students has submitted the assignment.
Each of the student have submitted the assignment.
Each of students has submit the assignment.
questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular and takes 'has'; 'students' stays plural after 'of'.

questions.prompt: Select the correct sentence:
options: I have been working here since 2022.
questions.explanation: An action starting in the past and continuing uses present perfect continuous.

questions.prompt: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'meticulous':
questions.explanation: Meticulous means showing great attention to detail.

questions.prompt: Passage: "Employers increasingly screen resumes with software before a human reads them. Candidates who write clear, keyword-aligned resumes pass this filter; others are rejected without review." Which statement is best supported?
options: Resume wording and keywords affect shortlisting
questions.explanation: The passage supports only the claim that alignment affects passing the filter.

questions.prompt: Passage: "A survey of 500 graduates found that those who completed at least two internships received 40% more interview calls, but the effect vanished for candidates without a clear project portfolio." In one short sentence, state the limitation of internships suggested by the passage.

rubric.modelAnswer: Internships only increase interview calls when a clear project portfolio supports them.

questions.explanation: A good answer links internship value to the presence of a project portfolio.

questions.prompt: Use the STAR structure (Situation, Task, Action, Result) in under 120 words: describe a time you solved a problem with a tight deadline.

rubric.modelAnswer: Situation: our mini-project demo was moved up by a week. Task: I owned the final module and the presentation. Action: I split remaining work into daily checkpoints, paired with a teammate on the UI bug, and rehearsed the demo twice. Result: we delivered on time and scored the highest in the batch.

questions.explanation: Scored on structure (STAR present), relevance and clarity.

questions.prompt: Write your two-minute self-introduction as you would speak it in an interview: education, one strength with evidence, one project, and why this role.

rubric.modelAnswer: Good morning Sir/Madam. I am a final-year B.E. student in Computer Science from ... My strength is structured problem solving - I cleared 250+ coding problems in six months. My project is a placement preparation portal built with Java and SQL. I am applying for this role because it lets me work on backend systems at scale, and I am ready to learn whatever technology the team uses.

questions.explanation: Scored on coverage of the four prompts, specificity of evidence, and clarity.

questions.prompt: Write a short email to a recruiter requesting a date change for your interview (under 100 words).

rubric.modelAnswer: Subject: Request to reschedule interview - [Name], [Role]. Dear [Recruiter], Thank you for the interview invitation on 14 October. I have my end-semester practical examination on the same day and would be grateful if the interview could be moved to 16 or 17 October. I remain available at your convenience. Regards, [Name], [Phone]

questions.explanation: Scored on subject line, clear request, reason, and professional tone.

questions.prompt: Topic: "AI tools reduce learning ability in students." Write your opening 90-second argument, taking a clear stand with two supporting points.

rubric.modelAnswer: I partially disagree with the statement. First, AI tools remove repetitive friction, so students spend their time on reasoning rather than syntax. Second, access to instant explanations helps students in under-resourced colleges close gaps. However, the benefit depends on how the tool is used: copying answers weakens learning, while questioning and verifying strengthens it. So the tool is neutral - the habit decides the outcome.

questions.explanation: Scored on clarity of stand, structure, evidence and balanced reasoning.

questions.prompt: Which normal form removes partial dependency of non-key attributes on a composite primary key?
questions.explanation: 2NF removes partial dependencies; 3NF removes transitive ones.

questions.prompt: Which query returns the second-highest salary from the Employee table?
options: SELECT MAX(salary) FROM Employee WHERE salary < (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM Employee)
SELECT salary FROM Employee ORDER BY salary DESC
SELECT MIN(salary) FROM Employee WHERE salary > MAX(salary)
questions.explanation: The maximum below the overall maximum is the second-highest.

questions.prompt: Which statements about database indexes are true? (Select all that apply)
options: They speed up reads on indexed columns
They slow down inserts and updates
They guarantee uniqueness in every case
Clustered indexes change physical row order
questions.explanation: Uniqueness needs an explicit UNIQUE constraint; the other three are true of indexes.

questions.prompt: Thrashing in an operating system is caused by:
options: Excessive paging due to insufficient frames
questions.explanation: When the working set exceeds available frames, the system spends its time swapping pages.

questions.prompt: Which scheduling algorithm can cause starvation of long processes?
questions.explanation: SJF keeps preferring shorter jobs, so long jobs may never run.

questions.prompt: Which layer of the TCP/IP stack is responsible for end-to-end reliability?
questions.explanation: TCP at the transport layer provides acknowledgements, ordering and retransmission.

questions.prompt: A client sends a request to a server on a new TCP connection. Which sequence of flags is observed?
questions.explanation: The three-way handshake is SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK.

questions.prompt: Which OOP concept lets the same method name behave differently for different object types at runtime?
questions.explanation: Method overriding dispatched at runtime is runtime polymorphism.

questions.prompt: In Java, which statement about the String pool and equality is correct?
questions.explanation: == compares references; equals() is overridden to compare content.

questions.prompt: In a common-emitter amplifier, the output voltage is:
options: 180 degrees out of phase with the input
questions.explanation: The collector current increases as the base drive increases, pulling the collector voltage down - hence inversion.

questions.prompt: In a four-stroke diesel engine, fuel is injected:
options: At the end of the compression stroke
questions.explanation: Compression ignition requires fuel injection at the end of compression when air is very hot.

questions.prompt: The accounting equation is:
questions.explanation: Every transaction keeps Assets = Liabilities + Equity in balance.
